title: Accordion Folder Story Arc Card Pack
audience: Families, homeschool groups, tutors, and adult-led writing tables for writers ages 7-11.
sessionLength: 16 printable accordion folder story-arc cards plus adult guide tools, arc routines, take-home arc slips, and optional adult prompts
safetyNote: No scary harm, no bullying, no romance, no weapons, no branded characters, no real child profiles.

cover.headline: Accordion Folder Story Arc Card Pack
cover.subhead: Sixteen accordion folder cards help writers sort a private fictional story arc into beginning, middle change, choice bridge, consequence, and ending return notes.

adultGuide.title: Accordion Folder Story Arc Adult Guide
bullets: Setup: print the cards, blank slips, and one accordion folder sheet, then label the paper pockets before writing begins: ____________________.
Beginning pocket: help the writer choose one pretend fact, object, place, or character note that starts the story arc: ____________________.
Middle change pocket: move one paper note forward when something gentle shifts in the fictional story world: ____________________.
Choice bridge: place a folded bridge slip between the middle change pocket and the consequence note so the arc movement stays visible: ____________________.
Ending return: use the final pocket for one detail that comes back calmly near the finish, then add a reset note behind it: ____________________.
Keep the whole activity adult-led, made-up, offline, paper-only, and broad enough for invented details only: ____________________.

arcRoutines.title: Beginning Pocket Sort
adultSteps: The adult opens the accordion folder to the beginning pocket and places one blank note inside: ____________________.
The child chooses one invented starter detail for the first pocket: ____________________.
The adult asks what the story reader should know first in this pretend world: ____________________.
The child writes or dictates the beginning pocket note on paper: ____________________.
arcRoutines.familyLine: The beginning pocket starts the story arc with: ____________________.

arcRoutines.title: Middle Change Lift
adultSteps: The adult rereads the beginning pocket note and points to the middle change pocket: ____________________.
The child chooses one small made-up change that can move the story arc forward: ____________________.
The adult asks how that change makes the pretend character notice something new: ____________________.
The child writes the middle change note and tucks it into the pocket: ____________________.
arcRoutines.familyLine: The middle change pocket moves the story because: ____________________.

arcRoutines.title: Choice Bridge Fold
adultSteps: The adult places one folded choice bridge slip between the middle change pocket and the next paper note: ____________________.
The child says one gentle choice the pretend character can make next: ____________________.
The adult asks what the choice connects from the middle change to the consequence note: ____________________.
The child writes the choice bridge line across the folded slip: ____________________.
arcRoutines.familyLine: The choice bridge connects the change to this next move: ____________________.

arcRoutines.title: Consequence Note Chain
adultSteps: The adult lays the consequence note after the choice bridge so the folder shows the next arc step: ____________________.
The child explains what happens because of the pretend choice: ____________________.
The adult keeps the consequence small, safe, and useful for the fictional arc: ____________________.
The child writes one consequence note and places it after the bridge: ____________________.
arcRoutines.familyLine: The consequence note follows the choice because: ____________________.

arcRoutines.title: Ending Return Pocket
adultSteps: The adult opens the ending return pocket and rereads one earlier folder note: ____________________.
The child chooses one detail from the beginning or middle that can return near the finish: ____________________.
The adult asks how the returning detail helps the story feel closed on paper: ____________________.
The child writes the ending return note and tucks it into the final pocket: ____________________.
arcRoutines.familyLine: The ending return pocket brings back this detail: ____________________.

arcRoutines.title: Reset Note Close
adultSteps: The adult checks the folder order: beginning pocket, middle change pocket, choice bridge, consequence note, and ending return: ____________________.
The child taps one pocket that should be remembered for the next paper pass: ____________________.
The adult writes a reset note that names where to restart in the accordion folder: ____________________.
The child closes the folder after adding one final pencil reminder: ____________________.
arcRoutines.familyLine: The reset note says to restart with: ____________________.

cards.middleChangePrompt: Middle change: make one compass point change, wobble, or reveal a new craft mark that complicates the goal: ____________________.
cards.choiceBridgePrompt: Choice bridge: let the character choose between two compass notes and explain how the choice keeps the arc aimed at the goal: ____________________.
cards.consequencePrompt: Consequence: write what happens to the craft project because of the chosen compass note: ____________________.
cards.endingReturnPrompt: Ending return: bring back the first compass goal and show whether the final paper note points closer to it: ____________________.
cards.arcFolderPrompt: Arc folder note: sort the compass goal, changed point, choice note, and ending return into the accordion folder: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: write the compass goal, one changed point, and one ending return sentence: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: save the Compass Craft Academy arc in the paper folder and add one new direction note later: ____________________.

cards.title: Greenhouse Gear Garden Story Arc Card
cards.arcSkill: reset the accordion folder with one ending return note
cards.useCase: Adult-led offline paper-only accordion folder card for finishing a Greenhouse Gear Garden story arc with a reset note: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Adult: keep the work private and offline, set out paper, pencil, this card, and an accordion folder for gear-garden arc pieces: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: Writer: with the adult, move the gear garden story from first problem to changed middle, choice, result, and calm return: ____________________.
cards.beginningPrompt: Beginning: write the first greenhouse gear detail, such as a turning wheel, label tag, or garden crank that starts the arc: ____________________.
cards.middleChangePrompt: Middle change: show one gear-garden part changing position so the character has to rethink the next paper step: ____________________.
cards.choiceBridgePrompt: Choice bridge: let the character choose one gentle repair, reset, or note-check that links the middle to the ending: ____________________.
cards.consequencePrompt: Consequence: write what changes in the greenhouse gear garden after that choice, using only made-up story details: ____________________.
cards.endingReturnPrompt: Ending return: bring back the first gear detail and write the reset note that closes the story arc: ____________________.
cards.arcFolderPrompt: Arc folder note: place the beginning gear detail, middle change, choice, result, and reset note into accordion order: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: write only the first gear detail, the changed part, and the reset note: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: keep the Greenhouse Gear Garden arc in the paper folder and add another ending return note later: ____________________.
